sources.excerpt: 2027 is approaching: what kinds of brands or industries will be skyrocketing in AI Search? AI Search / GEO.what_happened: I like it!. I like it! Brij Pandey (@LearnWithBrij) 🚨 A Netflix engineer just open-sourced the fix for the most…

sources.name: VeryWellVersed
sources.excerpt: I like it!. I like it! Brij Pandey (@LearnWithBrij) 🚨 A Netflix engineer just open-sourced the fix for the most expensive problem in AI: wasted tokens It's called Headroom, and it might be the smartest fix to high token usage Your agent reads a 10,000-token log file to find one error. You paid for all 10,000 tokens. The answer needed 1,200. Headroom sits between your agent and the LLM and compresses everything before the model sees it. JSON, code, logs, RAG chunks, each gets its own specialized compressor.
sources.author: @VeryWellVersed

sources.name: lilyraynyc
sources.excerpt: ChatGPT appears to be adding new disclaimers to its answers to help users make better decisions, especially in categories that are easy to manipulate. I’ve been tracking a long list of B2B software prompts in @peec_ai. Of ~700 ChatGPT answers, 82 included some kind of disclaimer in the past week, and 19 specifically warned users about who writes the rankings and reviews that ChatGPT draws on. ChatGPT is cautioning users about: ❌ Vendors ranking themselves in their own comparison pages ❌ Publishers that are affiliated with one of the brands they review ❌ Entire categories where many comparison articles are written by companies selling those products (cough, AI visibility tools) ❌ Sponsored…
